questions.q: Consider two physical quantities $A$ and $B$ related to each other as $E = \dfrac{B - x^{2}}{At}$ where $E, x$ and $t$ have dimensions of energy, length and time respectively. The dimension of $AB$ is

From the dimensional checking of the equation, we can say the dimensions of \left[B\right] = \left[x^{2}\right] = \left[$L^{2}\right]$

And dimensions of \left[A\right] = \left[x^{2}\right] \left[$tE\right] = \left[$L^{2}\right]\left[T\right] \left[ML^{2}T^{- 2}\right] = 1 \left[MT^{- 1}\right]$

Required value, \left[$AB\right] = \left[$L^{2}M^{- 1}T^{1}\right]$

$

questions.q: If force $( F )$, velocity $( V )$ and time $( T )$ are considered as fundamental physical quantity, then dimensional formula of density will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The dimensional formula of force is

$F = MLT^{- 2}$

The dimensional formula of velocity~is

$V = LT^{- 1}$

The formula for density is~

~Density $= \dfrac{M}{L3} = ML^{- 3}$

Comparing the density dimensions with the assumed fundamental quantities in the question,
$ML^{- 3} = \left[F\right]x\left[V\right]y\left[T\right]z ⇒ ML^{- 3} = \left[MLT^{- 2}\right]x\left[LT^{- 1}\right]y [ T{]}^{z} ⇒ ML^{- 3} = M^{x}L^{( x + y )}T^{- 2x - y + z}$

Comparing the exponents,
$x = 1 . . . ( i ) x + y = - 3 . . . ( ii ) - 2x - y + z = 0 . . . ( iii )$

Solving equations (i), (ii) & (iii), we get

$y = - 4, z = - 2$.

The dimensions of density $= FV^{- 4}T^{- 2}$.

questions.q: If $L, C$ and $R$ are the self inductance, capacitance and resistance respectively, which of the following does not have the dimension of time?

questions.q:
The equation of a circle is given by $x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}$, where $a$ is the radius. If the equation is modified to change the origin other than $( 0, 0 )$, then find out the correct dimensions of $A$ and $B$ in a new~equation :

\left(x - At\right)2 + \left(y - $\dfrac{t}{B}\right)$2 = a^{2}$

The dimensions of $t$ is given as~ \left[T^{- 1}\right]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Principle of Homogeneity states that dimensions of each of the terms of a dimensional equation on both sides should be the same. Then,

\left(x - At\right)2 + \left(y - \dfrac{t}{B}\right)2 = a^{2}$

For first term,~

\left[At\right] = \left[x\right] ⇒ A \times \dfrac{1}{T} = L$

$∴ \left[A\right] = T^{1}L^{1}$

For the second term,

\left[\dfrac{t}{B}\right] = \left[y\right]$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{T\left[B\right]} =L$

$⇒ \left[B\right] = T^{- 1}L^{- 1}$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement (I) : Planck's constant and angular momentum have the same dimensions.

Statement (II) : Linear momentum and moment of force have the same dimensions.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The dimensions of the required quantities can be written as

$E = hν ⇒ \left[$h\right] = \left[E\right] \left[ν\right] ⇒ [ h ] = \left[{ML}^{2}$T^{- 2}\right]\left[T^{- 1}\right] = \left[{ML}^{2}T^{- 1}\right]$

$\begin{cases}[ L ] & = & \left[mvr\right] \\ & = & \left[M\right]\left[{LT}^{- 1}\right]\left[L\right] \\ & = & \left[{ML}^{2}T^{- 1}\right]\end{cases}$

$\begin{cases}[ p ] & = & \left[$mv\right] \\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } \left[$M\right]\left[{LT}^{- 1}\right]\\ & = & \left[{ML}^{1}T^{- 1}\right]\end{cases}$

\begin{cases}[$τ ] & = & \left[Fr\right] \\ & = & \left[{MLT}^{- 2}\right]\left[L\right] \\ & = & \left[{ML}^{2}T^{- 2}\right]\end{cases}$

where, $h$ is Planck's constant, $L$ is angular momentum, $p$ is linear momentum and $τ is moment of force.

From the above analysis, it can be concluded that Statement I is true, but statement II is false.

$
